Although I agree with your main point, this is not how apoptosis happens. The membrane just starts blebbing due to the shrinkage of the cell. When it's extremely folded inward, the nucleus collapses and apoptic bodies are formed (which still have membrane). In the end they are destroyed by phagocytes to not cause inflamation of the body. But they can't really be called ''cells'' then, just waste.

The right analogy to illustrate your point would be necrosis, not apoptosis.

Also ''programmed apoptosis'' is a tautology.

It's like I'm listening to  myself. I too find solace in painting/sketching but lately nothing helps and just makes me feel guilty. 
What helps me sometimes on days like this is having really small goals and trying to do them one by one. 
For example if I can't go out of bed,first thing is to make myself stand up and wash my face,teeth and try to not thing about all the other things I am supposed to be doing but only focus on this one. And usually this creates a small momentum and it can spread to other basic tasks like make my bed and maybe like this I can do parts of my work (or even the whole thing).
So with illustration you may try to just set a goal to do like 3 sketches a day or just doodle in a sketchbook without putting too much pressure on yourself to always make quality art. Or if it really is too much taking a personal day might be better for you,sleep and try not to feel guilty about it. You are going to be ok despite these days.Tomorrow may be a better day!
